title: Add TUI skill routing, presentation, and explicit invocation
objective: Route exact /skills to an interactive launcher while preserving scoped /skills subcommands, dynamic suggestions, hidden developer metadata, and unambiguous explicit invocation in the TUI without introducing a new modal framework.
context: Complete one low-conflict slice of the accepted live skill catalog and cache-preserving design.
The worktree is shared and dirty; only owned_files may be modified.

source_evidence.note: Developer-context initial catalog and progressive disclosure inspiration.
Live discovery, visibility overrides, and skill lifecycle inspiration.

include: Route exact /skills with no arguments to SkillsMenuLauncher; route /skills list/show/set/reset/enable/disable/refresh through the existing text command backend.
Route unknown non-builtin /name to user skill invocation only when unambiguous and user-invocable.
Keep off and managed-denied skills unavailable.
Keep internal developer catalog messages out of the visible user/assistant transcript while retaining their model context.
Put every new user-visible routing/surface string behind semantic i18n keys with translations for all supported languages.
Define a small SkillsMenuLauncher contract so task_30 can own the direct interactive checklist without changing command semantics.
exclude: Do not modify production files owned by another task.
Do not add dependencies or perform unrelated refactors.

implementation_steps: Wire the exact-command launcher split, minimal command events, dynamic slash suggestions, and SkillInvoker configuration.
Filter internal developer catalog messages from normal transcript projection.
Add the launcher/open callback boundary used by the later interactive list task.
acceptance_criteria: Exact /skills opens SkillsMenuLauncher once; /skills subcommands still route through the shared text command and present the same effective state.
Manual-only remains user-invocable but hidden from model discovery.
Same-name collisions require a qualified stable selector.
Developer catalog messages are not rendered as assistant replies or user prompts.
All new user-visible copy uses semantic i18n keys and the active runtime language.
The launcher contract can open a future interactive skills surface without introducing a dependency on its concrete state type.
risks: repl_tui.go is heavily modified; keep changes limited to routing and dependency injection.
dispatch_prompt: Implement TUI /skills text routing, dynamic suggestions, hidden developer catalog projection, and explicit user skill invocation using existing backends. Do not build a new modal or change shared command/tool production files.
notes_for_assignee: If verification exposes a defect in another owner's production file, report the exact failing test and owner task; do not patch across ownership boundaries.
